messages.subject: prediction with state-space model
parts:
Dear all, 

I have mean rain data for 12 month, for each of the 57  measurement stations, so in total 684 events. 

After I fitted my model with the following formula:

formula<-rain~-1+Intercept+f(field ,model=spde, group = field.group, 
                                                                         control.group = list(model="ar1")) 

I want to predict the mean rain for the 13 month so January of the following year. Should I set up another stack with 

stack.pred<-inla.stack(data=list(rain=NA), .... with A.pred the locations of the 57 measurement stations?

If yes, how do I implement the new month as it would be group 1 again (groups equal to months), or do I need to introduce group 13?

Or do I need to simulate from the estimated values I get after the fitting process?

Appreciate your answer!

All the best,
Corinna

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] prediction with state-space model
parts:
Hi,

for the basic version of this type of prediction you need to include
the prediction months in the original model, so yes, you need to add
group 13 as part of the model itself.
You can do this by specifying 13 months to inla.spde.make.index(), and
you also need to specify this when calling inla.spde.make.A() to make
it setup the correct "group model" structure.

Finn
